But the detail is built by CALLING final_status AGAIN (:148), not from the statuses resolve_hosts already measured: (a) every no-candidate shard fires 3 EXTRA real curls (10s each) that are not injectable through the `probe=` seam, so the exact line this PR exists for cannot be unit-tested without a network -- I tried, it went to the network; (b) final_status maps any non-zero rc to None (verified by subprocess stub: 302/rc=28 -> None, 000/rc=7 -> None, 200/rc=0 -> 200), so the measured digest 302/rc=28 'followed redirect then CDN timeout' renders in the FAIL line the same as a connect refusal (None); the rc that distinguishes them is not printed. Fix: have resolve_hosts return (label, url, code, rc) and build the detail from those results once; print code/rc for each host (e.g. hf-mirror=302/rc=28, www.modelscope.cn=000/rc=7). That reuses the injected probe and makes the discrimination the docstring promises actually visible and tested.
2) SUCCESS PREDICATE: ==200 IS CORRECT FOR THIS PROBE; THE GAP IS rc COLLAPSE, NOT 206. Do NOT widen to {200,206} here -- this is a HEAD probe (curl -sIL); 206 is a Range-GET-only status and a HEAD cannot return it (measured live on both mirrors: -sIL final=200). final_status already fail-closes on curl rc (rc!=0 -> None, never ==200), so there is no fail-OPEN: 302/rc=28 can never be accepted as a host. The real defect is only the unreadable detail in #1. (Flagging because applying the {200,206} rule literally to a HEAD probe would be wrong; it belongs to a ranged-GET gate.)
3) PROXY IS NOT DEFAULTED -- the one arm this PR keeps for reachability is inert on digest. Neither the probe (final_status, no -x/--proxy) nor the transfer (_CURL_BASE, no -x) injects a proxy; they only inherit http(s)_proxy if the operator exported it. grep -n -- '-x|--proxy|DEFAULT_PROXY|sys-proxy' over the file = 0 hits, while scripts/probe_source_urls.py:35 defines DEFAULT_PROXY=http://sys-proxy-rd-relay.byted.org:8118 and the rebuild doc :322 probes THROUGH it. Consequence on the measured box: huggingface.co is 000 without proxy / 200 with, so the third failover entry can never serve there and the two mirrors are the entire chain -- the PR documents this as accepted ('reachability changes; keep the entry') but it contradicts the existing repo convention that this exact corporate proxy is the default for source probing. Decide explicitly: either reuse probe_source_urls.DEFAULT_PROXY for probe+transfer (so the hf.co arm is real), or state in the docstring/PR why env-only proxy is intended and DEFAULT_PROXY is not the default here. (1) ROOT CAUSE CORRECT: the pre-fix site is a fixed sleep plus ONE sample -- origin/main:scripts/card_claim.py:2032 time.sleep(1.5) then :2033 table = _ps_table(). A forked child must be SCHEDULED and on a loaded runner loses that race, so the table came back empty and every world assertion read the t=0 state; the empty list then made the ORPHAN-SHELL negative case unable to fail. Evidence cited by the commit (same sha green as a pull_request run, red as a push run, 1 of 262 targets) is consistent with a scheduling race, not with a code defect. (2) FIX CORRECT, and each call site polls the condition its own caller needs rather than a longer sleep: _await_ps is defined at scripts/card_claim.py:1567 with the deadline as a CEILING over the reported state, the same shape as wait_for_device at :241-247 ('THE WAIT AND THE CHECK ARE ONE CONDITION'). Sites: :2070 polls >= 2 descendants (the ambiguity refusal needs two candidates); :2441 idle >= 1; :2287 polls the REVERSE condition (the children are gone) so a kill that has not been reaped cannot read green; :2581 and :2689 and :2850 each >= 1; :2809 polls for the reparented row (ppid == 1); :3213 passes sample=_cvd because its condition is 'the child is VISIBLE to ps', a different reader from the process table. (3) GUARD DIRECTION CORRECT at scripts/card_claim.py:2274 (bool(kids) and not any(...)). MEASURED, four mutants on CPU: shipped 155/155; _job_descendants forced to return [] reddens 8 cases; disabling the ORPHAN-SHELL detection itself reddens 2; REMOVING the bool(kids) guard alone leaves 155/155 green, and A+guard-removed reddens the same 8 as A alone. So the guard's contribution is NOT visible in a BUG count -- with kids == [] the guarded form is red and the unguarded form is green, i.e. it flips 'the world never formed' from a silent pass into a failure, which is the direction asked for. A count of reddened cases cannot see that; the world-formedness of the case is what tests it. NO BLOCKING FINDING. task: PR 651 review: harness raw-string three docstrings (py3.12 SyntaxWarning), genA
artifact: scripts/harness.py @ ac6d1921809751c91009b74dfccd4a493b7253a7 (blob d0479f16ffb6ee806cb08ece43a09ac2bd06c7b2)
finding:
Review pass on ac6d1921 (artifact: the 3-line diff read in a detached worktree at that exact sha, plus an independent minimal-repair test; gate `pr_merge_gate.py 651` run).

The change is exactly what the body claims: three docstring openers `"""` -> `r"""` in `scripts/harness.py`, nothing else. I verified it against the compiler rather than against the scan, and the discriminating test is the one that settles the count.

**The claim "exactly these three" is correct, and I proved it by construction.** Under `python3.12 -W error::SyntaxWarning`, the merge-base copy (`f11fbb65`) fails to compile at line 5633 (`invalid escape sequence '\w'`); the PR head compiles clean. Then I took the OLD file and flipped ONLY those three openers to raw: it goes clean too. So no fourth site exists -- which is the assertion a "fixed 3 of N" claim needs and the body did not have.

**What I checked independently:**

| claim | how | result |
|---|---|---|
| old fails, new is clean at 3.12 | `py_compile` on both, `-W error::SyntaxWarning` | old `SyntaxError` line 5633, new CLEAN |
| 3.13 also clean | same | CLEAN |
| the three sites are the ONLY ones | minimal repair of the 3 openers on the old file | CLEAN -> no fourth |
| rendered text unchanged | AST `get_docstring` over both revisions, all functions | **0 of 517 docstrings changed** |
| the file emits no warning today | `warnings.catch_warnings(record=True)` + `compile()` | 0 SyntaxWarnings |
| gate | `scripts/pr_merge_gate.py 651` | `GO: 3 passing, 2 skipped`, rc=0 |

**One thing worth recording, because it shows how a review can go wrong here.** My first independent scan (a regex over non-raw string tokens) reported **7** invalid escapes, not 3, which looked like the PR had under-counted. It was my scan that was wrong: `scripts/harness.py` contains *doubly*-escaped sequences in prose (`r"-\\s*run:\\s*"` written inside a docstring, where the source really has two backslashes and the escape is valid). A regex cannot tell `\\s` from `\s` when it matches on the second backslash, and my scan's reported line numbers were token-start lines rather than the escape's own line, which is what made the two flagged "docstrings" (`_ci_explicit_paths`, `prereg_amendment_keys`) look untouched when I read them. The compiler is the only ground truth for this question; the scan was an instrument answering a different question than the one I asked it.

**Non-blocking, for whoever touches this next:** `warnings.catch_warnings(record=True)` around `compile()` reports 0, so a future regression that reintroduces a non-raw invalid escape in a docstring would be caught by the compiler only at *compile* time. There is no check asserting the file stays warning-free under 3.12, and this PR is the moment that would have been cheap to add. Not required for this change -- the fix is complete without it.

Verdict: approved. Nothing blocking. Merging with `--merge` once this row is in, per the handoff.

A job-level group does NOT exempt a job from the workflow-level group; ci.yml:26-28 sets group ci-${ref}-${event_name} with cancel-in-progress true, and a workflow_dispatch on the same ref is in that group, so the next dispatch cancels the previous one's jobs regardless of what each job declares. WHY IT MATTERS: the design's independence argument rests on '6-10 SEPARATE dispatches on independent runners', and whatever cancelled run 35868801042 was NOT its own matrix (fixed) -- which leaves the next dispatch. So (1) dispatch the next run only after the previous one's four cells have COMPLETED, or the earlier dispatch is silently truncated and its tally loses cells; a cancelled cell is a MISSING observation, neither green nor red, and nothing in the artifact names it as missing. (2) For true dispatch independence the fix is the WORKFLOW-level key: add run_id to ci.yml:27's group for the workflow_dispatch event. NOT claiming the 0922 conclusions are void -- the arms that completed did run on their own runners and the t2/oneDNN-on signal is supported by the 0/6-vs-6/6 contrast -- but the sample size is 'cells not cancelled by a later dispatch', so the denominator must come from the artifacts rather than from the number of times the button was pressed. No such file or directory' rc=3; shaped-but-unparsable line 'WATCHDOG PARSE ERROR ... missing loss/gnorm' rc=3; live with a log that never appears 'WATCHDOG READ ERROR ... did not appear within 3.0s' rc=3. THE BLOCKING DEFECT: main()'s live path is `f = open(args.log)` with NO .seek() anywhere in the file (grep -c seek = 0), so it feeds the detector every pre-existing line before reaching the tail; the log it is pointed at is the run's own append log and a resume under the same --name reuses it. So the sequence this PR is built for is pathological -- the run resumes, the log already contains the 12640 divergence that is the reason the watchdog exists, the watchdog opens it at offset 0, fires on the HISTORICAL divergence, and SIGTERMs the newly started run; today that surfaces as rc5 if it starts before torchrun, but with the other launch ordering or a watcher started seconds after the run it kills a healthy resume at step ~12010. Same class as the stale-stamp problems in this repo: the tool trusts a file whose content predates its own start. FIX: --once has --from_step and the live path needs the same floor -- start from EOF (f.seek(0, os.SEEK_END)) for a pre-existing log, or require --from_step in live mode; the ~900s --ready_wait for a not-yet-existing file is correct handling of the launch race and needs no change, the bug is only the pre-existing-file case. ONE MORE, NON-BLOCKING: rc4 staleness measures file position not log progress -- last_seen is updated on EVERY line read including non-progress lines, so a log that keeps emitting anything while training hangs never hits --max_stale; feeding last_seen only on a parsed progress line would make exit 4 mean what its name says. NOTED NOT BLOCKING: the loss arm gates on len(self.losses) == maxlen so a short log cannot fire it (deliberate, correct); resolve_torchrun_pids shells pgrep -f torchrun then filters by token adjacency so the exact-PID discipline and the NUL matcher are right, with t_cmdline_nul_separated covering the live-caught bug including the worker-not-launcher and trailing-digit cases; the AGENTS.md row, the pre-commit SELFTEST_FILES entry plus the ced_diverge_watch.py -> test trigger, and the ci.yml line are all present and consistent, and I ran the selftest: 'selftest pass: 8', rc=0.
